title: Time and quantity
summary: How long, how many, and how much.

questions.clue: This is a period of ten years.
questions.note: A hundred years is a century and a thousand is a millennium. Decade is stressed on the first syllable.

questions.clue: This is a period of two weeks.
questions.note: A contraction of fourteen nights. It is common in British English and almost unknown in American English.

questions.clue: This is the word for a group of twelve.
questions.note: Thirteen is a baker's dozen, from the practice of adding one loaf so as not to be caught selling short weight.

questions.clue: This is the fixed time by which a piece of work has to be finished.
questions.note: It originally meant a line around a prison camp that prisoners were shot for crossing, which explains the grimness of the word.

questions.clue: This is the larger part of a group, more than half of it.
questions.note: The smaller part is the minority. A vast majority is more than half by a wide margin, not a separate quantity.

questions.clue: This word describes something that happens once every year.
questions.note: Biannual is famously ambiguous, meaning either twice a year or once every two years, so careful writers avoid it.

questions.clue: This is the amount that is left over after everything needed has been used.
questions.note: The opposite is a deficit or a shortfall. Surplus is the neutral word and excess often suggests too much.

questions.clue: This word describes two things happening at exactly the same moment.
questions.note: The adverb is simultaneously. Concurrent is more common for events that merely overlap rather than coincide exactly.

questions.clue: This is the word for something that happens again and again at regular intervals.
questions.note: Periodic carries the sense of a fixed interval. Occasional means now and then with no pattern at all.

questions.clue: This word describes something that lasts for only a very short time.
questions.note: The opposite is permanent. Fleeting and transient are the more literary choices and both answer the clue.
